bug_description.original: A buffer overflow exists in the amazon video dissector.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read in `ndpi_check_amazon_video`. The staged 81-byte witness is an IPv4/TCP packet whose IPv4 total length is `0x0051` and whose TCP data-offset nibble is `15`, so `ndpi_init_packet_header()` computes `payload_packet_len = 61 - 60 = 1` and points `payload` at the final byte of the input, `0xFE`. The generic TCP dispatcher only requires `payload_packet_len != 0`, so the flow reaches `ndpi_search_amazon_video()` and then `ndpi_check_amazon_video()`. Vulnerable `amazon_video.c` checks only `packet->tcp != NULL` before comparing a four-byte TCP signature `FE ED FA CE`; it never requires `packet->payload_packet_len > 4` first. Because the sole payload byte matches the first signature byte, evaluation of `packet->payload[0] == 0xFE` succeeds and the next comparison reads `packet->payload[1]` one byte past the 81-byte input allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `READ of size 1` at `src/lib/protocols/amazon_video.c:39`. The staged fix wraps the TCP/UDP signature checks in `if(packet->payload_packet_len > 4)`, preventing this short-payload path from dereferencing beyond the buffer.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled payload length later violated by the amazon_video signature check.
source.value_from: The staged 81-byte `poc` is an IPv4/TCP packet with IPv4 total length `0x0051`, so the earlier L4 parser yields `flow->packet.l4_packet_len = 61` after the 20-byte IP header. The TCP data-offset nibble in the witness is `15` (`0xFC` high nibble), so this statement computes `payload_packet_len = 61 - 60 = 1`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Origin of the attacker-controlled bytes consumed by the crashing signature comparison. With the witness's 60-byte TCP header, this pointer lands on the final input byte, `0xFE`.

root_cause.var: packet->tcp, packet->payload_packet_len, packet->payload[0], packet->payload[1], packet->payload[2], packet->payload[3]
root_cause.description: The TCP signature branch requires only `packet->tcp != NULL`; it does not enforce any payload-length predicate before reading four signature bytes.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds an outer `if(packet->payload_packet_len > 4)` around both the TCP and UDP signature checks. On the witnessed path `payload_packet_len` is only `1`, so this missing guard is the source-level obligation the vulnerable code omits.

sink.description: ASan crash site. This comparison reads the second TCP signature byte even though the witness supplied only one payload byte.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` at `src/lib/protocols/amazon_video.c:39:8` in `ndpi_check_amazon_video`, and the faulting address is exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 81-byte input allocation.

parser_admitted.description: The flow has already passed generic packet parsing and the TCP payload dispatcher, so execution enters the amazon_video dissector on the staged witness.
parser_admitted.note: The amazon_video dissector is registered for `NDPI_SELECTION_BITMASK_PROTOCOL_TCP_OR_UDP_WITH_PAYLOAD`. Because `payload_packet_len` is `1` rather than `0`, the generic dispatcher still reaches this call.

fine_trace.note: In the TCP branch, the parser derives the payload extent from attacker-controlled header sizes. For the staged witness the earlier L4 parser yields `flow->packet.l4_packet_len = 61`, and the TCP data-offset nibble is `15`, so this assignment produces `flow->packet.payload_packet_len = 1`.
This points `payload` at the first byte after the 60-byte TCP header. In the witness that address is the last byte of the 81-byte input, `0xFE`, so only `payload[0]` is in bounds.

The generic TCP dissector dispatcher only rejects empty payloads. Because step 1 made `payload_packet_len = 1`, this guard passes and the still-unknown flow is dispatched into payload-based TCP protocol callbacks, including amazon_video.

fine_trace.var: packet->tcp, packet->payload_packet_len, packet->payload[0], packet->payload[1], packet->payload[2], packet->payload[3]
fine_trace.note: The TCP Amazon signature check is entered on a non-null TCP packet and immediately reads four payload bytes. The vulnerable source never checks `packet->payload_packet_len > 4` first, even though step 1 established that the witness has only one payload byte.

The sole in-bounds payload byte is `0xFE`, so the first signature comparison succeeds. Under C's left-to-right short-circuit evaluation, execution therefore advances to the next byte comparison instead of stopping here.

This reads the second signature byte even though step 1 established that only `payload[0]` exists. The address is exactly one byte past the 81-byte input allocation, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read at this line.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the faulting address at 0 bytes to the right of the 81-byte vector allocation that holds the staged `poc` bytes.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, patch.diff, and reproduction_report.json

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `if(packet->payload_packet_len > 4)` before either four-byte signature check. On the witnessed path `payload_packet_len` is `1`, so the fixed code excludes the protocol and never evaluates `packet->payload[1]`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the exact 81-byte witness saved by Stage 01. It is an IPv4/TCP packet with total length `0x0051`, a TCP data-offset nibble of `15`, and a one-byte payload whose only byte is `0xFE`. When the saved vulnerable run processes this buffer, `ndpi_init_packet_header()` computes `payload_packet_len = 1`, the dispatcher still reaches the amazon_video dissector because the payload is non-zero, `packet->payload[0] == 0xFE` succeeds, and the next signature comparison reads `packet->payload[1]` past the end of the buffer.

format.name: 81-byte IPv4/TCP packet with one-byte Amazon-video prefix
format.contract: An IPv4/TCP packet that `ndpi_detection_process_packet()` accepts, whose IPv4 total length and TCP data offset produce exactly one payload byte, and whose sole payload byte is `0xFE`. This witness-specific combination makes the TCP Amazon-video signature check accept the first comparison and then read `payload[1]` even though the payload extent is only one byte.
